jordan: Heads up — saw repeated GPU burst spikes from tenant 'partners-x' in eu-west this morning. Telemetry shows short-lived PCIe DMA bursts + kvcache miss storms, pushing host p99 up. Dump below.

jordan: ```
filter tenant=partners-x | metric=pci_dma_ops | group=host | p99>200ms | kv_miss_rate>0.25
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z host-az3 p99=312ms kv_miss=0.34 egress=12MB/s
2026-03-20T09:14:15Z host-az3 p99=298ms kv_miss=0.41 egress=9.4MB/s
```

sophia: thanks. is this noisy neighbor (hot bin) or just a pathological workload? any CPU/egress/NVLINK counters spiking?

jordan: CPU looks normal, but nvlink/dma counters are spiky. pattern = many tiny requests (seq_len=1) causing kvcache churn. likely a bursty bot or test harness.

liam: we've seen similar in us-east with tiny-chat workloads. Proposal: create a scratchpool (ephemeral slice) for bursty tenants that routes them to a soft-isolated runtime with strict egress policing and reduced NVLINK exposure.

maya: detection heuristics we can use: 3 bursts in 10m triggers 'burst-prone' tag. heuristics candidate: p99>200ms AND kv_miss_rate>0.3 AND egress_bytes_s>10MB for >=60s. add 5m hysteresis to avoid flapping.

jordan: agree on hysteresis. rollout plan: canary in eu-west-2, route new burst allocations to scratchpool with nvlink disabled and a write-through cache policy. fallback to main pool if we see regressions.

alloc-bot: alloc-bot: created policy scratchpool-ephemeral:v1 -> {egress_police=1MBps, nvlink=false, kv_cache_mode=write-through, preemptible=true, canary_region=eu-west-2}

liam: cost thought: scratchpool will add ~0.8% to infra spend for short term but should drop tail latency for co-tenants by ~30-40%. also opening path for aggressive caching/quantization later to reduce token cost.

sophia: OK let's run the canary. jordan can you open a PR with the heuristics, the policy, and a dashboard (kvcache misses, host p99, nvlink ops)? I'll schedule a 30m follow-up after canary start.

jordan: on it — PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4312 includes alert rules, rollout steps, and rollback criteria. starting canary at 09:30 UTC, will post updates here.

maya: +1
